newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juncker hopes for stability pact deal by end-June.
newsitem.headline: Juncker hopes for stability pact deal by end-June.

text.p: Luxembourg premier Jean-Claude Juncker said on Tuesday he hoped the European Union could find a solution to the impasse over a stability pact before the end of this month.

"I hope the French find the courage to finalise their position before the (June 16-17) Amsterdam summit," he told reporters as he arrived for a meeting of the European People's Party (EPP), a grouping of mainly Christian Democrat politicians.

The EPP leaders, including German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi, Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene, Spanish Foreign Minister Abel Matutes and European Commission president Jacques Santer, were meeting ahead of the Amsterdam summit next Monday and Tuesday to discuss NATO enlargement and the EU's inter-governmental conference (IGC).
The summit had been expected to approve the stability pact, an integral part of monetary union aimed at keeping budget deficits tight after the euro-launch.
But France on Monday said it needed time to study the pact further before approving it.
